styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Country music halls, studios and the art museum.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Hot chicken, meat-and-three plates and honky-tonk bars.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Civil War sites, the Parthenon and the state capitol.

stays.why: Walk to Broadway honky-tonks, the Country Music Hall of Fame and the riverfront. Noisier and pricier on weekends.
Trendy and walkable, a short ride from downtown. Good restaurants and bars, easy highway access.
Quieter, near the studios and Vanderbilt. Close to midtown restaurants; a short drive downtown.
Best value and the local food and bar scene. Five to ten minutes by car or rideshare to downtown.

food: Try Nashville hot chicken: crispy fried chicken brushed with cayenne paste. Ask for the mild level first; the hottest is very hot.
Look for a meat-and-three: pick one meat and three vegetable sides, a Southern lunch staple, often under $15.
Broadway honky-tonks have live music most afternoons and evenings; many have no cover charge, but tip the band.
Brunch and biscuits are a local ritual; expect queues at popular spots on weekend mornings.
Prices vary widely. Budget about $15–25 for lunch and $30–60 for dinner per person, more downtown on weekends.
more_time: Add a day for the Grand Ole Opry and a backstage tour; check show nights on the day.
History fans can swap an afternoon for The Hermitage, Andrew Jackson's plantation home, a short drive east of the city.
Families can add a morning at the Adventure Science Center or a walk in Centennial Park around the full-size Parthenon.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the music sights, hot chicken and a Broadway night; add a third for the Opry or The Hermitage.

month_notes: January is the coldest month: highs near 9°C, lows around -1°C. Pack a warm coat. About 12 rain days.
February stays cold, highs near 12°C. Indoor music venues are the safe bet. Around 13 rain days.
March warms to highs near 16°C with cool nights. Expect about 14 rain days, so bring a rain jacket.
April is pleasant: highs near 20°C, lows around 9°C. Good for walking. About 12 rain days.
May is warm and green, highs near 26°C. Comfortable evenings. Around 13 rain days.
June turns hot: highs near 30°C, lows around 20°C. Plan outdoor time for mornings. About 14 rain days.
July is the hottest and wettest month: highs near 32°C and about 17 rain days. Carry water and expect afternoon storms.
August stays hot and humid, highs near 30°C. About 15 rain days. Go easy outdoors at midday.
September is still warm, highs near 28°C, but rain drops to about 9 days. A good shoulder month.
October is the best month: highs near 23°C, lows around 12°C, about 9 rain days. Great for walking and patios.
November cools to highs near 16°C with about 9 rain days. Bring layers for cool evenings.
December is cold, highs near 12°C and lows around 3°C. About 11 rain days. Festive downtown lights are worth an evening.

climate_guide.summary: Humid subtropical: hot, sticky summers with afternoon storms, and mild-to-cold winters. Spring and autumn are the sweet spots.

items.title: Best time: April to May and September to October
items.text: Highs around 20–28°C with comfortable evenings. Ideal for walking downtown and outdoor music.

items.title: Summer is hot and humid (June to August)
items.text: Highs near 30–32°C with muggy air. Do outdoor sights in the morning; rest indoors at midday.

items.title: Summer storms
items.text: July and August bring the most rain days, around 15–17. Storms are often short but heavy; carry a small umbrella.

items.title: Winter is cold but short
items.text: January highs near 9°C and lows around -1°C. A warm coat and layers are needed for evening walks.

items.title: Rain is spread through the year
items.text: Most months see 9–17 rain days. Spring has more rain days than autumn, so pack a light rain jacket.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light breathable clothes and sunscreen for summer; a rain jacket; a warm coat and layers for December to February; comfortable shoes for walking downtown.

transit.best: Walk downtown; use rideshare or a rental car for everything else.

modes.text: No metro or tram. Don't plan around rail inside the city.
MTA buses cover downtown and the airport. Route 18 links BNA to downtown hourly, about 35 minutes.
Taxis are common downtown. Uber and Lyft both operate, with dedicated airport pickup areas.
A private car is the main way around. Highways run 55–70 mph but slow in traffic.
Downtown is walkable. Outside it the city sprawls and sidewalks are patchy.
The Music City Star commuter train runs from Riverfront Station to Lebanon. Useful for commuters, not most sights.
Bikes and scooters work for short downtown hops.
